The test image shows a soybean field with irregular, patchy areas of yellowing and browning plants scattered across an otherwise green canopy. This "hot spot" pattern — circular to irregular patches of chlorotic/stunted plants — is the hallmark field-level symptom of Soybean Cyst Nematode. 

Key observations:
- Field-level view with scattered yellow/brown patches (not row-following)
- Plants are yellowed/stunted but not dead/wilted
- Irregular patch distribution typical of nematode population clusters in soil
- No signs of sudden wilt or stem-level symptoms visible
- Pattern differs from SDS (which tends to follow rows) and Phytophthora (which causes more complete plant death)
